page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core operations. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng falls into the bottom 10%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are categorized as weak. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU scores all landing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also demonstrate average performance, as do Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.e4.4xlarge offers a high memory density of 8.0 GB per core, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The shared CPU allocation and older Intel Xeon architecture suggest a lower-tier hardware profile with moderate resource density. This server is suitable for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and lightweight language model inference using small models, whereas it is poorly suited for single-threaded tasks or larger LLM inference workloads.
